p1:main.reviewer: Codex native executor — actual source/content/browser review
p1:main.evidence: All requested subparts, original boundaries, concepts/first line/steps/answer/pitfall checked against current question. Independent answer evidence: Count the forward cyclic index distance from the slot before the first item (front) to the last item (rear). If rear>=front the distance is their difference; otherwise it wraps across M and equals M-front+rear. The reserved slot makes front==rear uniquely empty and maximum count M-1. The branch version avoids an unnecessarily large intermediate sum in the modulo expression. O(1) time and auxiliary space.

p2:main.reviewer: Codex native executor — actual source/content/browser review
p2:main.evidence: All requested subparts, original boundaries, concepts/first line/steps/answer/pitfall checked against current question. Independent answer evidence: Reversing in makes its oldest item the top of out. Existing out items must be consumed before transferring later in arrivals, preserving FIFO. Each item is pushed/popped at most once per stack, so enqueue O(1), dequeue worst O(n), amortized O(1).

p3:main.reviewer: Codex native executor — actual source/content/browser review
p3:main.evidence: All requested subparts, original boundaries, concepts/first line/steps/answer/pitfall checked against current question. Independent answer evidence: Append normalized alphanumeric characters at one end, then repeatedly remove and compare the two ends. Punctuation and spaces never enter the deque; case folding makes A and a equal. An empty or one-character normalized deque is a palindrome. radar compares r/r then a/a and leaves d.

p4:main.reviewer: Codex native executor — actual source/content/browser review
p4:main.evidence: All requested subparts, original boundaries, concepts/first line/steps/answer/pitfall checked against current question. Independent answer evidence: Both front and rear identify the unique node after an enqueue into empty. Removing the unique node leaves neither valid endpoint. Resetting rear prevents a dangling pointer to freed storage and restores the empty-queue invariant front==rear==NULL.

p7:main.reviewer: Codex native executor — actual source/content/browser review
p7:main.evidence: All requested subparts, original boundaries, concepts/first line/steps/answer/pitfall checked against current question. Independent answer evidence: An empty deque has no previous tail to patch and must establish both endpoint pointers. On the next insertion, the old tail links right to the new node and tail advances; new node already links left to the old tail and right to NULL.

p8:main.reviewer: Codex native executor — actual source/content/browser review
p8:main.evidence: All requested subparts, original boundaries, concepts/first line/steps/answer/pitfall checked against current question. Independent answer evidence: If new head is NULL, tail must also become NULL so empty endpoints agree and no dangling tail remains. Otherwise the new head left link must become NULL so it does not reference the removed node. Omitting the test and unconditionally dereferencing head crashes/causes UB on the final deletion; omitting updates leaves stale tail or dangling llink.

int get_count(const QueueType *q){ if(q->rear>=q->front) return q->rear-q->front; return MAX_QUEUE_SIZE-q->front+q->rear; }

p5:main.conclusion:
Original if/else: clock1 1->0, B still waiting; clock2 0->2, B starts at clock2 with waiting time 1; clock3 2->1.
After replacing else with an independent if(service_time==0): clock1 1->0->2, B starts at clock1 with waiting time 0; clock2 2->1; clock3 1->0->0, since remove_customer sees an empty queue and returns 0.
